author: FX.Sniffer
text:
I've posted this in another topic and thought its time to bring it here.

Supply and Demand zones presents a stack of unfilled orders either offers or bids.

Stacked zones presents stacked groups of unfilled orders (limit orders), in every zone there are unfilled stacked orders on top of each other.

As Sam Seiden explained in a webinar - Unfilled orders moves market prices, the chart line/candles/bars represent filled/executed orders and the white space around it represent the unfilled orders (limit orders) thus we need to focus on the big unfilled orders (limit orders).

What I'll explain here based on my understanding of the market, so is the attached chart. The following example applies to the stacked zones as well as to stacked orders inside a zone.

In case of a supply zone scenario, offers shall be stacked above each other (the wider the zone the more orders at different prices) logically the majority would sell high and this is why unfilled orders would increase higher into the zone, and with every return of price to the zone the sell orders are decrease/consumed.....now this doesn't mean the smart or big money would be sitting at the highest prices....nope not necessarily....they are the smart money and they know where to set and distribute their offers...well, it could be among the highest offers and "for example" this is where a compression ends, or it might be among the lowest offers and this is when we see a spike or a quick touch of the zone's lower edge then price bounce and drops for a long distant before returning back and starts pressuring or forming ascending triangle to consumes the entire zone.

Of course the strength of buyers and sellers plays a big role in this process every time it happens, thus comes the importance of how did the price leave the zone, and how is price returning to the zone.

I hope I made it simple and clear.

P.S. The attached chart present Buy/Sell limit orders.

I thought I could make a contribution to your analysis on gold.

In this post

 www.acegazette.com/en/community/ace-foru...l.html?start=25#8511

I try to answer why did price react where it did. The only answer I could find was that it reacted from an ignored monthly supply intersecting with weekly D/S zone. It is such an important zone that I thought price would have to go even higher in order to come back down. That's why I thought the QM wouldn't work. I didn't say anything at the time because I didn't want to influence your plan/decision.

In your analysis you also highlight a nice pin bar being a fake out. That looks to me like a reaction to a RBD and it would have been a great entry.

What's interesting is that I don't see that RBD on your charts and it only shows up on my charts when I select Ask price as opposed to buy price!!

I would appreciate if I could hear your thoughts on these points.

Cheers

Let me clear one thing I'm not an awesome trader at least not yet and I do a lot of mistakes, the S/D method helped me to dig deeper into the market structure in order to understand the order-flow and I'm still in middle of the road. I do researches, readings, brainstorming then apply it on charts. I'd love if other traders join in (its traders helping traders), and it would've been easier if I had the chance to learn directly from a pro, trading floor, or a financial institution but unfortunately never had the chance. Tyoon is doing the same in a different way.

Now if you look at post #78 the H4 chart you'll see a marked supply zone and the same candle closed as a spinning top (a pinbar on H1) the pinbar played its role nicely and I didn't consider the RBD on LTF, I was paying attention to the close of PB below the resistance level and below the close of previous swing high as a fakeout and I don't have the same feed as yours, the same RBD you're pointing at has a high of 1730.02 and the PB high is 1731.83

As for the QM it was a stupid analysis cuz there was a bigger invert QM and very clear on H4 (see below chart) and its coming at the end of down trend which is a perfect location for an invert QM or H&S, and of course if you have two QMs one big at a good location and the other is smaller and an important level above it, which one has a stronger effect? lesson learned
